title: Starter Immersion Activity Log & Skill Transfer Protocol
body:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook for new joiner immersion that emphasizes cross-functional skill transfer, lightweight mentor rotations, and an action-first 10/30/90 velocity map. Designed as a practical activity log + protocol for managers and mentors to capture evidence and handoffs mid- and end-of-cycle.

Status and usage notes:
- Draft > internal review > publish as template in /confluence once we get two pilot cohorts through (target Q1 2026).
- Keep intentionally minimal: checklist + evidence prompts + 2x templates (mentorship rotation schedule, handoff record).
- Use with Hire Intake Form (linked artifact) and role competency profile.

High-level flow (one-liner):
1) Hiring manager completes brief intake + expected 10/30/90 outcomes.
2) People Ops assigns primary mentor + two rotation mentors (optional cross-pod).
3) Week 1-2: immersion + barrier removal; Week 3-4: paired tasks + micro-deliverable; Month 1-3: ownership transitions + assessed evidence.

Checklist: Week 0 (pre-start)
- [ ] Manager completes intake + success criteria (attach to candidate record).
- [ ] Access provisioning requested and verified (okta, slack, repo).
- [ ] Primary mentor assigned and first sync scheduled (30m pre-start).
- [ ] 10/30/90 skeleton added to role doc and shared with new hire on day 1.

Week 1 (orientation & discovery) - activity log fields
- Day 1: welcome, org overview, key docs + 1:1 with manager (evidence: meeting notes link).
- Day 2-5: shadow flows: product PR walkthrough, infra runbook read, customer support triage (evidence: 3 notes / quick wins).
- Mentor action: create 3 micro-tasks for new hire to complete by EOW (assign in GH/Asana).

Week 2-4 (paired work + small ownership)
- Goal: ship one small scoped change end-to-end.
- Pair with rotation mentor for half days (schedule: Tue/Thu weeks 2 & 3).
- Evidence capture: PR link, post-merge mini-retro (1 paragraph), bug/regression checklist.

30-day checkpoint (manager + mentor + hire)
- Template questions to capture (use in meeting):
  - What did you ship? link(s)
  - Which systems/repo paths do you now own?
  - 3 blockers we removed and how
  - Confidence (1-5) on core competency areas
- Outcome: update 10/30/90 doc; decide if more rotations needed.

60-day focus (deepening + cross-pod collaboration)
- Expand ownership: delegate incident runbook ownership or product story end-to-end.
- Introduce hire to 1 upstream and 1 downstream partner and set a paired deliverable.
- Evidence: documented runbook edits, cross-team design note.

90-day (handoff & leveling evidence)
- Handoff slate: what the hire owns, how to escalate, playbook links.
- Manager rating + mentor evidence (use rubric below).
- Decide: business impact mapping + next-sprint owner list.

Mentor Rotation Protocol (practical rules)
- Rotation length: 2 weeks per mentor (minimum), overlap with primary mentor at boundaries.
- Number of mentors: primary + up to two rotation mentors (one technical, one product/ops).
- Mentor responsibilities: 30m/wk structured check-in, make sure new hire has 2 concrete tasks, add evidence to activity log.
- Replace mentors when availability < 50% for the rotation period.

Activity Log template (to be copied into hire doc):
- Date | Activity type (shadow/pair/ship/meeting) | Owner/mentor | Artifacts (links) | Outcome/notes | Follow-up actions
- Keep entries terse (1-3 lines) — this is for evidence, not a diary.

Handoff Record template (end of 90d)
- Role owner: [name]
- Systems owned: [list, repo paths, runbook links]
- Known gaps & mitigations: [short bullets]
- On-call/alerting responsibilities: [yes/no + notes]
- Primary escalation path: [names + slack / pager duty]

Evidence-first Interview Rubric (for hiring decisions focused on transferability)
- Emphasis: candidate has demonstrable habits for learning and shipping (not just answers).
- Rubric axes (1-5):
  - Problem decomposition (can break fuzzy problems into testable subproblems)
  - Deliver-ops (history of delivering small, observable results)
  - Cross-team communication (explicit handoffs & doc examples)
  - Learning velocity (how quickly they adapt to new stacks)
- Evidence sources: take-home microtask, PR examples, past runbooks/diagrams, manager references.
- Hiring decision rule: 3 axes >= 3 and at least one >=4, OR strong compensating evidence in past deliverables.

Quick templates (copy/paste)
- 10/30/90 skeleton (to paste into role doc):
  - 10 days: orientation goals + 3 micro-tasks to ship
  - 30 days: own at least one service/feature; close 3 issues
  - 90 days: independently own one customer-facing flow or infra surface

- Manager pre-start intake (short):
  - Role outcome in 90d (one sentence)
  - Critical systems touched (list)
  - Proposed mentors (names + why)
  - Key compliance or security needs

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we require a standardized evidence folder per hire in GH or Confluence (pros/cons)?
- Pilot with two roles (infra eng and solutions eng) before generalizing.
- Add a short onboarding survey at day 30 to capture blocker signals (auto trigger via slack workflow).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally more operational than the big onboarding playbook — meant to be a fillable working template.
- Lean on people-ops to coordinate mentor nomination and capacity.
- If approved, I'll spin this into a confluence template + a Slack workflow to auto-create the activity log.

History/Context:
- Inspired by feedback from recent hires that 'too many ambiguous tasks' slowed velocity; this flips to "what can you ship" as the primary signal.
- Aligns with org thesis: ramp = removing blockers + enabling fast, observable ownership.

Last edits: Aisha — tightened mentor rules, added rubric.
